closure_requirements: An implementation reference (diff or commit), or an explicitly named supported-scope limitation.
A failing-before / passing-after regression where a regression is applicable.
Exact environment, source revision, fixture snapshot and command recorded.
A current acceptance result; a report predating the relevant code change cannot close the item.
Review by someone other than the implementer; self-reported completion is a claim, not closure.

issues.finding: SessionToken::decode_verify (crates/strivo-web/src/auth.rs:55-57) compares the HMAC with expected_sig.as_slice() != actual_sig.as_slice(), a short-circuiting compare. The same file's ApiKey::matches (:104-115) is deliberately constant-time with a documented rationale about not leaking length. The session path does not meet its own module's stated standard. Remote exploitability against HMAC-SHA256 is low; the inconsistency is the defect.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Use the hmac crate's verify_slice, constant-time by construction. Closure: the code change, with the record stating that timing-oracle absence is argued from the primitive used and was NOT established by timing measurement.

issues.finding: No invariant test asserts that every registered route is auth-gated, and no such property is checkable from the current test structure (see S03). The scan behind S01/S02/S06/S07 was a regex over .route(...) registrations matching 68 of 153 registrations repo-wide (routes/api.rs yielded 26 of its 53). The remaining ~85 registrations were checked by no method at all. More unauthenticated routes may exist; this manifest does not claim to have found them all. UPDATE 2026-09-06 (revision 3): the sweep now EXISTS on branch remediation/web-auth (commit d46d2a9), inventories 166 route registrations (55 always-compiled + 111 creator-only) and asserts 401-for-bogus-key against an explicit public allowlist. Reviewer ran it. It is only PARTIALLY effective: 49 registrations (13 always + 36 creator) return 422/400 because axum's body extractors reject a malformed body BEFORE the handler's auth check runs, so the sweep marks them 'inconclusive' rather than passing them. Those 49 are proven neither gated nor ungated by any method. UPDATE 2026-09-06 (revision 6), branch remediation/auth-sweep: FIXED (commit cac829b): ALLOWLIST renamed KNOWN_PUBLIC; both sweeps now hard-ASSERT on inconclusive as well as on violations, where inconclusive was previously only eprintln'd and silently absorbed. Reviewer's mutation test confirms the assertions fire.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Send a schema-valid body for each mutating route so the request reaches the handler and the auth check actually runs, converting all 49 inconclusive results into real assertions. Then resolve the red-branch problem: the two sweeps currently FAIL by design because they found real gaps (S13/S14/S15), and CI gates on `cargo test --workspace`. Do NOT #[ignore] them — that is skip laundering. Convert to an exact-match assertion against a declared known-unauthenticated list, so the suite is green, every listed gap is visible, and any NEW ungated route fails the build. Acceptance: zero inconclusive results, and the known-gap list is empty. REVIEWER NOTE on the guard's limits: the sweep asserts COMPOSED behaviour, so wrongly adding a route to KNOWN_PUBLIC is NOT caught when that route's handler still performs its own check_key/check_dual (verified by mutation: allowlisting /api/v1/channels kept the sweep green because the handler rejected the request anyway). That is defense in depth working, not a hole — but it means the sweep guards the middleware, not the allowlist. An allowlist error on a route WITHOUT a handler check is caught.

issues.finding: README.md is uncommitted at audit entry with 185 insertions and 337 deletions (git diff --stat). The rewrite drops the AUR badge and restates edition scope and platform-support claims. It was NOT adjudicated against current behaviour in this pass. Any release built from this tree would ship doc claims no review has checked. UPDATE 2026-09-06: REVIEW COMPLETE — no unsupported claim found. Every checkable assertion in the rewrite was traced to source: Windows support and named-pipe IPC (src/ipc.rs:207), Task Scheduler enable (crates/strivo-bin/src/cli.rs:28), `strivo status` exit 3 (main.rs:1028,1043), the search/pull/repair/--daemon-only subcommands (cli.rs:54,60,106,32), both build commands, Twitch EventSub and YouTube WebSub implementations, release-archive contents (.github/workflows/release.yml) and all six linked docs. NOTABLY the reverse drift was found instead: the CURRENTLY COMMITTED README's 'Windows unsupported' badge is the stale claim, not the rewrite. One completeness note, not an inaccuracy: the rewrite drops the AUR badge and section while packaging/aur/PKGBUILD still exists in-tree — an operator decision on whether AUR is still maintained.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Review the rewrite against current behaviour and commit or revert it. Closure: the tree is clean, or the diff is reviewed with its capability claims spot-checked against code. Until then every README capability claim is unverified.

issues.finding: DESIGN.md and CLAUDE.md are deliberately untracked — .gitignore:45-51 lists them under '# Internal docs (kept local only)' — and `git ls-files --error-unmatch` confirms neither is known to git. DESIGN.md exists only in the operator's working tree (13,992 bytes). Meanwhile the TRACKED ROADMAP.md:126-128 cites DESIGN.md as normative ('DESIGN.md §Web UI Theme + Typography'), and the project's own workflow mandates 'Always read DESIGN.md before making any visual or UI decisions.' Consequence: no fresh clone, no CI run, and no `git worktree` has the document that governs every visual decision. OBSERVED IMPACT this session: three remediation agents were dispatched into git worktrees, all of which lacked DESIGN.md; the SPA agent correctly reported it could not find the file and proceeded from in-file CSS precedent instead. Its inferred focus-ring colour (var(--primary)) happens to match DESIGN.md:92, but that was luck, not compliance. UPDATE 2026-09-06: the safe half is implemented (ROADMAP.md now states DESIGN.md is gitignored and absent from every clone, CI run and worktree) without deciding the underlying question; .gitignore untouched and no ignored file was staged. IMPLEMENTER'S RECOMMENDATION, for the operator: track DESIGN.md — it is cited as normative by both CLAUDE.md and ROADMAP.md, contains design tokens and typography rather than secrets, and its absence has already caused three agents to be dispatched blind. Fallback if it must stay private: strip the normative citations instead.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Decide between two coherent positions and implement it: either track DESIGN.md (dropping the privacy goal) so its normative references resolve, or keep it private and remove the normative citations from tracked files, replacing them with a stated 'design authority is maintained out-of-tree' note. Whichever is chosen, any workflow that dispatches work into a git worktree must copy the untracked design authority in explicitly. Acceptance: no tracked file cites a document a clone does not contain.

issues.finding: Auth is checked INSIDE handler bodies, after axum's extractors have run. The S08 sweep demonstrates the consequence: 49 of 166 route registrations (13 always-compiled, 36 creator-only) answer a bogus-credential request with 422 Unprocessable Entity or 400 Bad Request — a body-shape rejection produced before the handler's auth check executes. Observed directly in the sweep output for, among others, POST /api/v1/settings/update, POST /api/v1/blocklist, DELETE /api/v1/blocklist, POST /api/v1/vods/download, POST /api/v1/channels/resolve and POST /api/v1/licence/activate. Two consequences: those 49 routes are proven neither gated nor ungated, and an unauthenticated caller can distinguish valid from invalid request shapes on routes they cannot otherwise reach. UPDATE 2026-09-06 (revision 6), branch remediation/auth-sweep: FIXED (commit 8a91381) via the preferred structural route: a require_auth middleware applied with .route_layer() on the merged guarded router. route_layer wraps each already-registered route directly, so it runs before that route's own Json/Query extractors — closing the whole 422-before-auth class at one point instead of per handler. The public websub route is merged AFTER the layer and so stays public, and the 404 fallback is untouched (router_unmatched_path_404s still passes). Sweep result: 0 violations, 0 inconclusive on both editions.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: The structural fix is to authenticate in middleware ahead of extraction rather than per-handler, which also removes the whole class of defect S01, S13 and S14 belong to — a handler that forgets the call. If per-handler auth is retained, every mutating handler must extract the body only after checking credentials. Acceptance: a bogus-credential request to every non-allowlisted route returns 401 regardless of body shape, proven by the S08 sweep with zero inconclusive results.

issues.finding: PVR-reachable UI depends on Creator-only backend routes. `GET /api/v1/plugins` and `GET /api/v1/plugins/chat/rooms` are registered in crates/strivo-web/src/routes/plugins.rs (:4383, :4505), and that whole router is merged only under #[cfg(feature = "creator")] (server.rs:122-123). But the SPA calls them from edition-agnostic code: API.chatRooms() at spa.js:5209, :6074 and :7368 (chat page, viewer, watch-page chat rail) and API.plugins() at :9084 and :10754. Surfaced while fixing S10 — the implementer had to move both definitions OUT of the creator strip blocks precisely because PVR code needs them. Reviewer traced the error handling: the chat page (:5207-5212) catches and renders a '⚠' error banner, the chat rail (:7368) catches and proceeds, and the info modal (:10754) catches and substitutes an empty list, so nothing crashes. The consequence is a PVR build whose chat feature always shows an error where the backend route simply does not exist.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Decide whether chat and the plugin index are PVR features or Creator features, then make both sides agree. If PVR: move those two routes out of the creator-gated plugins router into an always-mounted router. If Creator: gate the calling UI so a PVR build does not present chat at all. Acceptance: in a real PVR build (the S04 real-server lane can drive this), opening the chat page produces a defined state with no failed request — not a caught-and-displayed error.
